Plan: plenum box 0.3×0.12×0.08 m, eight swept runners (30 mm straight + 90° arc of R=60 mm turning upward, so the port face sits 90 mm out from the plenum wall), inlet as a 70 mm disc on the end wall. Build in metres from the start.

```python
from build123d import *
import numpy as np, os, subprocess

L, W, H = 0.300, 0.120, 0.080          # plenum length, width, height
D_IN = 0.070                            # throttle inlet diameter
D_R, R_BEND = 0.038, 0.060              # runner diameter, centreline bend radius
REACH = 0.090                           # port face distance from plenum wall
Z_AX = H/2                              # runner axis height on plenum wall
STRAIGHT = REACH - R_BEND               # straight lead before the bend
XS = [L*(2*i+1)/8 for i in range(4)]    # 4 evenly spaced stations
print("stations", XS, "straight", STRAIGHT)

plenum = Pos(L/2, 0, H/2) * Box(L, W, H)

def runner(x):
    p0 = Vector(x, W/2 - 0.012, Z_AX)          # start 12 mm inside the plenum wall
    p1 = Vector(x, W/2 + STRAIGHT, Z_AX)
    ln = Line(p0, p1)
    arc = JernArc(start=p1, tangent=(0, 1, 0), radius=R_BEND, arc_size=90, plane=Plane.YZ)
    path = Wire([ln.edge(), arc.edge()])
    prof = Plane(origin=p0, z_dir=(0, 1, 0)) * Circle(D_R/2)
    return sweep(prof, path)

runners = [runner(x) for x in XS]
runners += [mirror(r, Plane.XZ) for r in runners]
fluid = plenum + runners
print("volume m^3", fluid.volume, "bbox", fluid.bounding_box())
```
I'll send that as a tool call.
JernArc has no `plane` kwarg here — I'll build the bend as an explicit three-point arc, which also lets me verify the radius numerically.
Re-emitting the full geometry cell, self-contained, with the bend as a three-point arc.
Geometry closes at the right extents. Now inventory the faces of the union so I can name patches from surface type and known port centres, not bbox position.
Numbers first: port discs, bend radius, inlet plane. Then build the two sheet faces that split the end wall into inlet disc + annulus.
Rectangle came in rotated; fix `x_dir`. Then group the faces into named patches.
Tessellate each face and write one STL per patch, then verify the welded union myself before meshing.
Closed, watertight union. Look at it before meshing.
Geometry is right. Now the case files: background blockMesh box plus snappyHexMesh with each STL as a named region.
Running snappyHexMesh now at the coarse base size.
blockMeshDict boundary syntax was wrong (extra parentheses). Rewriting it.
Mesh exists. Check patches and volume against the CAD, and look at it.
Coarse mesh is sound (Mesh OK, volume 0.00399 vs CAD 0.004007). Now refine to level 2 (≈2.5 mm, ~15 cells across a runner) and rerun.
Mesh is good. Verify patch areas against geometry and render it.
Patch areas match (within faceting). Final look at the mesh.
Quick self-check of STL orientation (signed volume of the welded union) before declaring.

Built and meshed. Summary:

**Geometry** (metres throughout, no scaling needed): plenum box 0.300 × 0.120 × 0.080 m; eight runners, four per side at x = 37.5, 112.5, 187.5, 262.5 mm (even 75 mm spacing), each a Ø38 mm tube leaving the plenum wall horizontally in ±y, 30 mm straight then a 90° bend of 60 mm centreline radius turning upward, so the flat port face lies 90 mm out from the plenum wall (y = ±150 mm) at z = 100 mm with normal +z. Inlet is a Ø70 mm disc on the x = 0 end wall.

**Measured from the built solid**: port diameter 0.038000 m (asked 0.038), bend centreline radius 0.06000 m (asked 0.060), straight lead outside the wall 0.0300 m, port reach from wall 0.090 m, inlet diameter 0.070000 m, total fluid volume 0.0040073 m³.

**Patches**, named on the faces as constructed/selected (by surface type and known port centres, never by bbox side), one STL each in `constant/triSurface`: `inlet`, `plenumWalls` (5 box faces + the end-wall annulus), `runnerWalls` (8 cylinders + 8 tori), and `portL1..L4`, `portR1..R4`. The welded union of all STLs has 0 free/non-manifold edges and positive signed volume (outward normals).

**Mesh**: blockMesh background 10 mm + snappyHexMesh surface level 2 (≈2.5 mm, ~15 cells across a runner), no layers. 95 312 cells, checkMesh "Mesh OK", max non-orthogonality 40.2, max skewness 0.62; mesh volume 0.0040019 m³ (0.13 % below CAD). Patch areas match geometry to ~0.4 % (circle faceting): inlet 0.003836 vs 0.003848, each port 0.001129 vs 0.001134.

**Not checked**: no boundary-layer cells were added (not requested), and I did not assess y+ or solver-side resolution; runner-to-plenum junction fillets do not exist in the description so the tubes meet the wall sharply.
